details.description: DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B is a 1.5-billion-parameter dense reasoning model that DeepSeek released in January 2025 alongside DeepSeek-R1, fine-tuning Alibaba's Qwen2.5-Math-1.5B on about 800,000 reasoning traces generated by DeepSeek-R1. It is the smallest model in DeepSeek's R1 distillation family, built to bring R1-style step-by-step reasoning to hardware too limited for the full 671B R1 model. DeepSeek's model card recommends running it without a system prompt at a temperature of 0.5-0.7, and notes the model can sometimes skip its own reasoning step. Both the model weights and DeepSeek's code are released under the MIT License.
advantages: Supports a 131,072-token context window, inherited from its Qwen2.5-Math-1.5B base, per its Hugging Face configuration file.
Scores 83.9% pass@1 on MATH-500, per DeepSeek's Hugging Face model card.
Scores 28.9% pass@1 on AIME 2024, rising to 52.7% with 64-sample consensus voting, per DeepSeek's model card.
Scores 33.8% pass@1 on GPQA Diamond, per DeepSeek's model card.
DeepSeek reports a CodeForces rating of 954 for this model, per its model card.
Released under the MIT License, permitting commercial use and further distillation, per DeepSeek's model card.
disadvantages: Scores 16.9% pass@1 on LiveCodeBench, the lowest of the Qwen-based models in DeepSeek's R1-distill family, per DeepSeek's model card.
DeepSeek's model card says the distilled models can skip their own reasoning step on some queries, which may require forcing the response to start with '<think>\n'.
Text-only reasoning model; its model card documents no vision or tool-use support.
use_cases: Lightweight chain-of-thought reasoning on resource-constrained hardware.
Coding assistance and code reasoning at small scale.
Research and experimentation with small-scale distilled reasoning models.

notes: Catalog's max_input/output tokens (131072) match this model's max_position_embeddings in its Hugging Face config.json, so no discrepancy. No maker source marks this model deprecated or superseded; it remains DeepSeek's smallest R1-distilled checkpoint from the January 2025 R1 release.
